title: Charge-Transfer Electronic Structure of NiX$_2$ (X = S, Se)
authors: Atsushi Hariki, Takaki Okauchi, Daisuke Takegami, Naoki Ito, Mizuki Furo, Ayako Yamamoto, Tomoya Higo, Satoru Nakatsuji, Masato Yoshimura, Takashi Mizokawa, Jan Kunes
abstract: We investigate the electronic structures of NiS$_2$ and NiSe$_2$ using density functional theory combined with dynamical mean-field theory (DFT+DMFT). A realistic electronic structure within DFT+DMFT was determined by optimizing the double-counting correction to reproduce experimental valence-band photoemission spectra. The validity of the present model is further confirmed by its successful description of the Ni 2$p$ core-level photoemission and Ni $L$-edge x-ray absorption spectra of NiS$_2$. Our results reveal a smaller charge-transfer energy than previously assumed, resulting in substantial ligand-to-Ni charge transfer and a reduced Ni local moment. We clarify how the relative position and interaction between the Ni upper Hubbard band and the antibonding chalcogen-dimer states shape the evolution of the low-energy electronic structure across the NiS$_{2-x}$Se$_x$ series.
summary: This paper uses advanced DFT+DMFT calculations to map the electronic structure of nickel dichalcogenides (NiX2). By fitting to experimental photoemission and XAS data, the authors revise the understanding of the charge-transfer energy, concluding that substantial charge transfer occurs from the chalcogen ligands to the Ni centers. This work provides a detailed picture of how orbital interactions govern the electronic properties across the NiS2-xSe_x solid solution.
main_problem: The study investigates the electronic structure and charge-transfer mechanism in nickel dichalcogenides (NiX2) to understand their insulating behavior and Metal-Insulator Transitions.
main_result: The calculations reveal a smaller charge-transfer energy than previously thought, leading to significant ligand-to-Ni charge transfer and a reduction in the Ni local magnetic moment.
method: The research employs Density Functional Theory combined with Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (DFT+DMFT) to model electron correlations.
model_or_system: The physical system is NiS2 and NiSe2 in the pyrite structure, with the solid solution NiS2-xSe_x being analyzed. A tight-binding model spanning Ni 3d, S/Se p\pi, and p\sigma states is used within the DFT+DMFT framework.
key_observables: Valence-band photoemission spectra (PES), Ni 2p core-level PES, Ni L-edge XAS, and the Ni local magnetic moment.
important_parameters: The double-counting correction ($\mu_{dc}$) is a key parameter determined by fitting to experimental PES data; the charge-transfer energy ($\Delta_{dp}$) is also crucial.
main_assumptions: The model relies on fitting the double-counting correction to reproduce experimental spectra, and simplified models are used to isolate orbital contributions.
figures_summary: Figures show DFT spectral densities for NiS2 and NiSe2, and simulated K-edge absorption spectra comparing results for different assumed charge-transfer energies.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using DFT+DMFT, calibrates the model against multiple experimental spectra (PES/XAS), derives key electronic parameters (like the CT energy), and then analyzes the orbital hybridization and spectral evolution across the NiS2-xSe_x series.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state materials, the use of DMFT to model strong local correlations and the detailed analysis of orbital hybridization and charge transfer mechanisms are highly relevant to understanding open quantum systems and correlated dynamics.
